title: South Carolina's 5th Congressional District election, 2026
description: The 2026 election for South Carolina's 5th Congressional District is an open-seat race to succeed incumbent Republican Rep. Ralph Norman, who left Congress to run for governor. The district spans northern South Carolina along the North Carolina border, encompassing all of York, Lancaster, Chester, Fairfield, Cherokee, Union, Lee, and Kershaw counties, plus portions of Spartanburg and Sumter counties. It has been a Republican stronghold since 2010, with Norman winning by 63.5% in 2024. The general election features Republican state Sen. Wes Climer, Democrat Mallory Dittmer, and Forward Party candidate Andy Kaplan, with the seat widely rated as Solidly Republican by nonpartisan forecasters.
polling_note: No public general-election opinion polls were found for this race as of mid-June 2026. The Cook Political Report rates the seat as 'Solidly Republican'.

candidates.name: Wes Climer
candidates.summary: Wes Climer is a Republican state senator from York County who has served in the South Carolina Senate since 2016. He won the Republican nomination for the 5th Congressional District unopposed and is running on an America First agenda focused on tax cuts, school choice, constitutional carry legislation, and federal spending reductions. Climer previously worked as a congressional aide in Washington and as a financial consultant before entering politics.

candidates.name: Mallory Dittmer
candidates.summary: Mallory Dittmer is a Democratic candidate and former corporate retail executive who spent 15 years in the fashion industry working with brands like Kate Spade and Coach. She became a political advocate and campaign consultant in South Carolina, helping seven candidates win local elections in 2024, and founded Community Advocates for Public Education York County. Dittmer won the Democratic primary on June 9, 2026, defeating Andrew Clough with 55.8% of the vote, and campaigns on affordability issues including healthcare, childcare, and grocery costs.

candidates.name: Andy Kaplan
candidates.summary: Andy Kaplan is a Forward Party candidate and healthcare professional with 30 years of experience in healthcare administration, medical sales, and community engagement. He and his wife Patty, a public school teacher of 27 years, moved to South Carolina 15 years ago. Kaplan is running on a platform of clean government, pledging to refuse PAC money, support term limits, and ban stock trading for members of Congress, and emphasizing bipartisan cooperation and practical policy solutions.
